questions: Shelter buildings in an earthquake or a strong hurricane
Which shelter buildings have been assessed for earthquake and hurricane-wind resilience, and which need a check before they are used after a strong event?
How would water, food, cots, fuel and medical supplies reach Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi if the harbours or airports close for several days, and who decides the order of shipments?
Which areas lose mobile phone service first in a long power outage or after wind damage, and how will warnings and shelter information reach them (radio, sirens, door-to-door)?
When a school is used as a shelter, how long can it stay open before classes must restart, and where do residents go next?

Could each county collect partner capacity (cots, meals, staff, vehicles, interpreters) with a county-run form such as Survey123, with no personal data, so the plan can show pledged capacity instead of 'confirm with partner'?

stress.not_no_shelter: This is not a statement that the area has no shelter: counties designate and open shelters for each event, and many public buildings are not on the 2026 list.

assumptions.people_per_trip: 20 people per vehicle trip (team assumption: the plan gives no value)
assumptions.outage: 0 days = the plan: outlets for people in shelter only

how.people_in_shelter: People in the risk area × shelter-seeking rate.
how.cots: One cot per person in shelter, rounded up (planning assumption: no published per-person cot factor is cited).
how.floor_sqft: 20 sq ft per person for stays up to 3 days, 40 sq ft beyond (Florida DEM 2010; past 14 days a team assumption).
how.water: 1 gallon per person per day (Florida DEM 2010) × days of stay.
how.meals: 2 meals per person per day (Florida DEM 2010) × days of stay.
how.toilets: 1 per 40 people for stays up to 3 days, 1 per 20 beyond (Florida DEM 2010).
how.outlets: 1 outlet per power-dependent person in shelter (HHS emPOWER-based estimate; team assumption). During a power outage: 1 charge a day for every power-dependent resident in the risk area, if that is more (team assumption, upper bound).
how.staff: Florida DEM (2010) ratios per shift: registration 1 per 165, dormitory 1 per 100, meals 1 per 110, mental health 1 per 250, health 1 per 200, security 1 per 100, sanitation 1 per 200 (each at least 1); children's area 1 per 12 children.
how.interpreters: People with limited English in shelter × each language's share of limited-English speakers (ACS PUMS 2019–2023). Each person may need an interpreter; it is not a count of interpreters.
how.support: People in shelter × the share needing support. Plan default: the share of people in shelter with a disability (ACS via CDC SVI).
how.trips: People in households without a car in the risk area ÷ people per vehicle trip, rounded up (an upper bound: not all will need a ride).
how.pets: Households in shelter × 44.6% with a dog and 26% with a cat (AVMA, 2020 data).
how.allocation: Each Census area's people in shelter go to the nearest usable 2026 site on the same island by drive time (Esri ArcGIS, normal traffic). Capacity is compared only when you enter it.

hub.maui_2013: Tsunami Safe Zones for Maui, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi date from 2013; the other counties' zones date from 2025. Check Maui County's current evacuation maps.
hub.pdc_note: 2009 reference capacity (American Red Cross Hawaiʻi State Chapter, Pacific Disaster Center data via a third-party ArcGIS Online copy; the PDC catalogue confirms the 2009 date): may be outdated. Use only as a starting point; confirm with the county.

sources.safe_zones: Tsunami Safe Zones (Hawaiʻi Statewide GIS; Hawaiʻi Island, Oʻahu and Kauaʻi zones 2025, Maui County zones 2013), simplified outline.
sources.fire: State Fire Risk Areas (DLNR Division of Forestry and Wildlife, 2007; boundaries confirmed 2022, via Hawaiʻi Statewide GIS), simplified outline. The plan's wildfire numbers use the FEMA National Risk Index; this layer is a comparison.
sources.flooded: Future sea-level-rise scenario (3.2 ft; State of Hawaiʻi SLR-XA), tested against 2026 sites: potentially flooded highways (Hawaiʻi Sea Level Rise Viewer, PacIOOS, via Hawaiʻi Statewide GIS). Chronic flooding later this century, not an event forecast.
